title: Germany Opens National Drone Security Research Center in Cochstedt After Leipzig Airport Bomb-Drone Incident
detail: Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, Research Minister Dorothee Bär, Saxony-Anhalt Minister-President Sven Schulze, and DLR Executive Board Chair Anke Kaysser-Pyzalla inaugurated the new Drone Security Technology Center at the German Aerospace Center's (DLR) Magdeburg-Cochstedt airfield on August 18, expanding the existing National Test Center for Unmanned Aircraft Systems. The facility, backed by over €10 million in funding and up to 40 new positions across sites in Cochstedt and Braunschweig, will develop and field-test technology to locate, identify, track, and counter unauthorized drones threatening airports, public events, and critical infrastructure under realistic conditions. The opening came roughly two weeks after a drone carrying explosives and a detonator was found near a Ukrainian Antonov Airlines cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle Airport, a major European air-freight hub used for NATO logistics. Dobrindt called malicious drone incursions part of the 'shadow war of the 21st century' and announced the federal police's counter-drone unit would double in size, from 150 to 300 officers.

media.caption: Officials inaugurate Germany's new Drone Security Technology Center at the DLR's Cochstedt airfield

title: Germany Boosts Ebola Aid to Democratic Republic of Congo by €11 Million
detail: Development Minister Reem Alabali-Radovan announced on August 18 that Germany is increasing its support for the Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of Congo by €11 million ($12.7 million), confirmed to dpa by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). Alabali-Radovan called the outbreak 'the worst Ebola outbreak in the country's history,' noting that ongoing armed conflict in eastern DRC is hampering healthcare workers' ability to reach infected populations. The additional German funding supports equipment provision, mobile laboratories, and training for healthcare workers, adding to Germany's existing Ebola-response commitments.

media.caption: Germany pledges an additional €11 million to fight the worsening Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo
